points: Background: after Yoshiyahu is killed, Nevuchadnetzar exiles King Yechanyah and the "craftsmen," which Chazal say were the talmidei chachamim and the elite, and makes Tzidkiyahu king. Yechezkel was among those exiled.
Yirmiyahu sees two baskets of figs. The good figs are the exiles in Bavel, whom Hashem will bring back. The bad figs are those left in Eretz Yisrael.
Why so harsh? After a terrible calamity they should have changed radically, and they didn't. They thought, "We're in Eretz Yisrael, so we're safe."
Eretz Yisrael is precious, but the land doesn't save you; Hashem does, and He demands proper behavior.
He calls it haunting: after October 7th, are we as a nation changing for the better or fighting among ourselves? Which basket of figs are we?
